[PyTorch GRUCell](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.rnn.GRUCell.html) computes r=σ(W_ir x+b_ir+W_hr h+b_hr), z analogously, n=tanh(W_in x+b_in+r⊙(W_hn h+b_hn)), then h′=(1−z)⊙n+z⊙h. Substituting q=g⊙h as the cell’s hidden argument changes every recurrent computation, including the direct carry: h′=(1−z)⊙n+z⊙g⊙h. Thus this is more than an additional candidate reset gate. By differentiation, ∂q/∂h=diag(g)+diag(h⊙g⊙(1−g))W_h; the complete Jacobian is J_GRU,h(x,q) times this matrix. The direct carry coefficient becomes z⊙g, introducing additional attenuation, although other derivative paths can compensate or amplify.

Recommendation precedents include [DIEN’s AGRU/AUGRU](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/4545/4423), which replace/scale the update gate, and [Contextual RNNs](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.07684), which modulate recurrent transformations. Neither is algebraically equivalent: AUGRU suppresses new updates while preserving old-state carry; the proposed gate suppresses the old state itself. A closer placement precedent outside recommendation is [GRU-D](https://arxiv.org/html/1606.01865), which decays hidden state before recurrent processing. These sources establish related gating mechanisms, not an exact recommendation precedent for this particular parameterization.

Algebraically, zero gate weights and bias b=logit(p) initialize constant retention p. Any finite sigmoid bias gives p<1: even p=0.99 contributes an extra 0.99^100≈0.366 factor along a 100-step carry path, so near-identity initialization systematically attenuates that path. Exact baseline recovery requires bypassing the extra gate with g≡1; no finite sigmoid initialization achieves it mathematically. Alternatively, reparameterize g=2σ(a) with zero weights/bias: initially g=1 and ∂q/∂h=I, with trainable gate gradients, but subsequent gains can exceed one. This recovers standard GRU behavior, not necessarily h′=h.
